## Goal

Everything a person sees on the way into Mostra and through a hosted page looks beautiful, feels like one product and works for everyone: signing in, linking a machine, approving a chat app, answering a hosted page on a laptop or a phone, and every page a link can end on. It follows Mostra's visual identity and Studio (D141), is accessible (WCAG 2.2 AA), and holds every security rule these surfaces already keep.

## Owned requirements

None: a maintenance or design unit owns no requirement (D152). Its progress report's evidence table has one row per item of its scope, each closed by a check through the real public interface (README §3), and the checks it adds extend their owners' rows.

## Scope

From [WORK_PACKAGES.md](../WORK_PACKAGES.md):

- one design pass over every page the open server draws outside an artifact, in Mostra's visual identity and Studio's tokens and faces (D141), accessible to WCAG 2.2 AA, on desktops and phones;
- the API origin's pages: sign-in with its providers, the development provider's name page, the device page (unsigned, signed in, approved, refused, an expired or unknown code), the consent page for a chat app (a registered client, a metadata-document client marked unverified, a loopback redirect's warning), "Answer as yourself", and every "Sign-in can't continue" page;
- the hosted shell's trusted chrome (`packages/shell`): the header and its sender line, the viewer chip, Submit and "Your answer was sent.", the footer, the report dialog, the paused notice, an operator's interstitial, the storage notice, the version banner and the submit refusals, with a header that holds together at phone width;
- the pages a link can end on: expired or revoked, under review, the owner's pages suspended, moving, a limit reached on view, an unknown host, a page that fails to load;
- one small template module for server-rendered pages: no script, a stylesheet served by the page's own origin or hashed, self-hosted faces (no third-party request), every string from one words file and every tenant or operator string escaped as text; published, so an operating layer outside this repository can build its own pages on the same template;
- the viewer-facing words of these surfaces, reviewed with Mirza (D149, D161).

Design detail for this package:

- A design unit: it owns no requirement. Its scope is the surfaces in WORK_PACKAGES.md, each in every state; its progress report has one evidence row per item of its acceptance evidence, each closed through the real interface, and the checks it adds extend their owners' rows (HY-09, SH-01 and SH-02 keep theirs).
- The specification spans this repository and the operating layer's own repository, worked in one session: the public half here is everything above; the private half (the operating layer's pages, mail and dashboard) is built outside this repository on this package's published template. Nothing of the private half enters this repository.
- **Research first:** read the design skills Mirza lists (web-design-guidelines, emil-design-eng, design-taste-frontend, high-end-visual-design, frontend-design, impeccable's references, and a few more found with find-skills) and note in a short brief what each adds, what is adopted and what is rejected; the brief is design input, never authority over the dossier or the brand.
- **Questions to settle with Mirza before building,** as one set with options and a recommendation: brand or Studio on Mostra's own pages; the open server's name and mark under a self-hoster's name; one source for the look shared with the operating layer (a published template it pins); dark mode; and the operating layer's dashboard base.
- **Caller first, two directions:** for each surface family (the API origin's pages, the hosted chrome, the end pages) write who meets it, from where, wanting what and on what device, then show Mirza two structurally different directions as screenshots at desktop and phone widths, and build the one he picks.
- **The hosted chrome keeps its rules and its tests:** the artifact can't reach, restyle or imitate it (WP-30's HY-09 suite and WP-07's forgery suite stay green, untouched); strict CSP with no inline script and Trusted Types; every tenant or operator string as text; no cookies on hosted origins; `Origin-Agent-Cluster`, CORP and `frame-ancestors` as D165 item 7 sets them.
- **Faces:** Figtree and Spline Sans Mono, SIL OFL 1.1, self-hosted from the page's own origin with the system stacks as fallbacks (D141 item 4), their licenses in NOTICE.

## Out of scope

- The review overlay and the shell's final pass beyond the chrome (WP-20); kit components (WP-18, WP-19); the marketing and docs sites (WP-26); CLI output.
- New behaviour: a defect found on the way is fixed with its test if small, or filed.

## Acceptance evidence

every surface and state photographed by a committed script in Chromium, Firefox and WebKit at 1280 and 390 pixels wide, committed as visual baselines; axe with no serious or critical finding on any surface; keyboard-only and screen-reader passes on sign-in and Submit; contrast AA in every mode; reduced motion honoured; long and hostile content (a 256-character name, a right-to-left name, an unbreakable title, a 1,000-character operator message) rendered as text without breaking the layout; a real phone over the tailnet (external); WP-07's forgery suite and WP-30's HY-09 suite green and untouched; `ci:full` green; Mirza's design review and his acceptance of the words.

Also: `pnpm check` green, diff reviewed, the progress report's evidence table complete for every owned requirement (README §3), the evidence matrix regenerated, docs and AGENTS.md current, and the report finalized after acceptance (README §4).

## Risks and notes

- The shell is one build for local and hosted pages: a change to its chrome reaches local viewers too, and every e2e suite that reads its words or markers must stay green.
- Self-hosted faces add bytes to the shell and the runtime bundle; subset them and keep the size budgets.

## Handoff

The templates and words every later surface uses; WP-20's final pass on the shell starts from this chrome. WP-16 follows.
